title: “I Am Responsible for the Aircraft’s Nervous System”: How 23-Year-Old Yevheniia Prepares Combat Aircraft for Missions
text:
Yevheniia serves in the 39th Tactical Aviation Brigade and is responsible for the operation of radio-electronic equipment on combat aircraft.
Before the full-scale war, she was preparing to become a medic, but after February 2022 she radically changed her profession and retrained for a technical specialty in military aviation.
Her story was published on the brigade’s page.
Yevheniia is originally from the Dnipropetrovsk region. She grew up in a family of a teacher and a security guard. Although there were no military personnel in her family, her parents supported her decision to join the army.
After the beginning of the full-scale invasion, the girl realized that she could not remain on the sidelines. Where medical protocols once existed, avionics schemes and algorithms of complex onboard systems appeared.
Now she works directly with aircraft and is responsible for communication systems.
“I am responsible for the ‘aircraft’s nervous system’ — the pilot’s communication with the command. Without this, successful execution of a combat mission is simply impossible”, — the servicewoman says.
According to Yevheniia, preparing an aircraft is teamwork where every check matters.
“We bring every little detail to perfection because we understand the price of this machine’s reliability”, — she says.
When the aircraft takes off, technicians feel a brief relief — the first stage of the mission has been completed. But the work does not stop: after returning, the aircraft must be inspected and, if necessary, immediately prepared for a new flight.
After two years of service, Yevheniia admits that aircraft have stopped being just machines for her.
Even outside service, when she hears the sound of an engine over the city, she involuntarily looks into the sky searching for the silhouette of a fighter jet.
In a team where most are men, the girl feels confident. She says the unit has become a second family for her.
Many more years of service lie ahead. Yevheniia’s greatest dream is a time when the roar of fighter jets will mean only training flights, not combat sorties. But for now — another equipment check and a new aircraft heading out on a mission.

title: Occupiers Strike the Front Line with Drones and Artillery: Kramatorsk and Druzhkivka Terrorized by Guided Aerial Bombs
text:

The situation on the Kostiantynivka axis was described during an ArmyTV stream on March 6 by Anastasiia Khaletska, head of the communications section of the 4th Separate Heavy Mechanized Brigade.
— It is more expedient for them to use aviation deeper into our territory, that is, against rear cities.
If we speak about our direction, Druzhkivka currently suffers the most from shelling, as well as Kramatorsk. Mostly these are guided aerial bombs.
Sometimes the intensity is such that several dozen GABs can fall in one city during a single night, — she said.
Meanwhile, on the front line the enemy strikes with artillery and unmanned aerial vehicles, especially searching for the positions of Ukrainian drone operators.
— If we talk about the front edge, the enemy mostly uses UAVs and artillery there.
For example, several months ago we observed a tendency on the Kupiansk axis where the enemy began to use artillery extremely actively.
Moreover, they used it in order to try to locate the take-off sites of our pilots.
Therefore, on any axis there are periods when enemy artillery begins to work quite actively.
But currently, most of the damage on the front line is inflicted by UAVs, — Anastasiia Khaletska reported.

title: Paratroopers rescued a severely wounded comrade near Pokrovsk using a robotic ground system
text:
As a result of an enemy mine explosion, the soldier suffered a partial amputation of his lower limb.
Footage of the rescue was published on the page of the 25th Separate Airborne Sicheslav Brigade of the Air Assault Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
On the Pokrovsk direction, paratroopers of the 25th Sicheslav Brigade of the 7th Rapid Response Corps together with fighters of the 68th Separate Jaeger Brigade named after Oleksa Dovbush carried out a joint mission to evacuate the wounded from the position.
The evacuation was conducted using the Bizon ground robotic complex.
The evacuation was complicated by heavy mining of the area and a large number of enemy drones in the sky.
The total route length was 24 km (12 km one way).
During the evacuation constant communication with the wounded soldier was maintained through the internal communication system inside the robotic capsule. However, during movement the robotic system was hit by an enemy FPV drone and communication with the wounded soldier was lost.
Silence filled the radio. Hope that the wounded soldier had managed to jump out of the capsule faded with every minute.
Imagine the commander’s emotions when a call from the pilot appeared on the phone screen.
“Commander, I’m alive. I didn’t receive any additional injuries. I managed to jump out and reached the position of a neighboring unit of the 68th Jaeger Brigade”, — the commander recounts.
Further evacuation was carried out by comrades. After being taken out of the kill zone, the wounded soldier was delivered to a stabilization point, where he received all the necessary medical care.
As the brigade notes, modern technologies, quick decision-making and the joint actions of neighboring units together form a coordinated system that today ensures the saving of lives.

title: Ukraine can help protect lives — President on the situation in the Middle East
text:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a meeting on the challenges for Ukraine and partners, as well as on our ability to help protect lives and stabilize the global market.
This became known on the evening of March 4.
“The Iranian regime, which is trying to preserve itself despite everything, creates obvious threats to all states in the region as well as to global stability.
No state near Iran can feel safe. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has practically stopped.
So far the Iranian regime does not demonstrate a real intention for honest diplomacy or fundamental changes”, — Volodymyr Zelenskyy said.
According to him, Ukraine is holding consultations both with partners in Europe and the United States and with countries neighboring Iran.
“Yesterday I spoke with the leaders of the UAE and Qatar. Today there were already conversations with the leaders of Jordan and Bahrain. There will also be talks with Kuwait and other countries in the region.
All of them face a serious challenge and speak about it openly: Iranian strike drones — the same ‘Shaheds’ that have been attacking our cities and villages and our Ukrainian infrastructure throughout the years of this war”, — the President noted.
According to his data, more than 800 missiles of various types and more than 1,400 strike drones have already been used by Iran in several days.
“It is Iranian drones and missiles that are the key threat to free navigation, and this destabilizes prices for oil, petroleum products and gas around the world.
Ukraine can help protect lives and stabilize the situation. Partners are addressing us about this”, — the President said.
He instructed the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine together with intelligence agencies, the Minister of Defense, our military command, and the Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council to present options for support for the respective states and to provide assistance in such a way that it does not weaken our own defense here in Ukraine.
“Our military possess the necessary capabilities. Ukrainian experts will work on the ground, and teams are already coordinating this.
And we are ready to help protect lives, protect civilians and support real efforts to stabilize the situation and restore, in particular, safe navigation in the region”, — Volodymyr Zelenskyy assured.
He added that Ukraine expects the European Union, European states and the Group of Seven to be active both in eliminating the terrorist capabilities of the Iranian regime and in protecting lives in the region and global stability.

title: “One of the dangerous factors is getting used to danger”: the story of an artilleryman with the call sign “Goodwin”
text:
His combat path began in the spring of 2022 with the destruction of enemy aviation as an anti-aircraft gunner, and today he continues the fight in artillery rec
The story of the fighter was shared on the page of the 44th Separate Artillery Brigade named after Hetman Danylo Apostol.
In the first hours of the bombing of Kyiv at the beginning of the full-scale invasion, he managed to evacuate his family from the capital. At that time his daughter was only one and a half years old.
The first weeks in the new place were spent solving everyday problems, as many people arrived at the house at the same time. At the same time, together with the local territorial defense, the man dug trenches and collected tires.
And already in March, Viacheslav and his brother-in-law were standing at the door of the military enlistment office.
Viacheslav spent the first year and another half of the second year “in the tree lines” as an anti-aircraft gunner. His task was to wait with a MANPADS for an enemy aircraft or helicopter.
However, later the man learned about the artillery reconnaissance unit, which appealed to him more in terms of interests and corresponded to his civilian skills.
Today he is already a squad commander working in the counter-battery warfare system. His main task is to operate special equipment that monitors enemy artillery guns.
Their coordinates are calculated in the central vehicle, of which he is the commander, and then transmitted further for the successful work of the artillery.
Viacheslav says that they have to work with equipment that was manufactured back in the 1990s. However, as it turned out, even when working with it, the background from his previous profession became indispensable.
“The most interesting thing is that although the equipment is from the last century, it is all digital. This complex operates on the same architecture as modern laptops or phones. It’s just that ours is modern equipment, and that one is equipment from the 1990s, when a computer was still called a computing machine”, — the serviceman explains.
Modern devices help the military in their work, and the materials for them mostly exist in English. Therefore, knowledge of a foreign language and the ability to work with specific software are critically important skills for artillery reconnaissance.
However, Viacheslav is convinced that much of the necessary information can actually simply be googled or obtained from open sources.
But while almost anyone can master technical skills, no one can change the weather conditions. And these are a key factor on which the effectiveness of the computing unit’s work depends: in unfavorable conditions, the reconnaissance radius significantly decreases.
“Then we can say that we are a bit blind. About 90% of the time during the year the conditions are favorable for work, but we cannot influence the rest. Although, you know, in IT there is such a symbol — a shamanic tambourine. One could knock on it so that the weather clears up”, — the commander jokes.
In addition to the weather, the intensity of enemy actions also affects the work of the unit. Servicing the equipment regularly is vital, but doing it under the constant surveillance of enemy drones is extremely difficult, Viacheslav shares.
The stability of the frontline is also important: if it moves too quickly, the effectiveness of reconnaissance decreases.
Most of the fighters at the position have been serving together for the fourth year already — many of them joined even before the full-scale invasion.
The commander says that such experience allows them to understand each other without unnecessary words.
“We have rubbed in with each other so much. Someone will always support you, someone will joke at the right time. We live like a big family, just not a very prosperous one”, — Viacheslav laughs.
But the main thing is that everything in the unit is based on communication, mutual trust and mutual respect, because without them any unit cannot exist.
“And ‘magic kicks’ are another important aspect of relationships in the unit. One of the dangerous factors is getting used to danger, when the level of stress stops being enough to keep you alert. Then the ‘magic kicks’ help. Everyone has gone through this more than once”, — the commander shares.
This is how the commander manages to remain calm despite the complexity of the work and constant threats. Because it is in the combination of critical thinking, professionalism and sincere humor that the resilience is born that allows them to effectively destroy the enemy.

title: “The scariest thing is transporting two tons of shells”: driver “Samolyot” told how he ‘flew’ into Myrnohrad

“I transport ammunition, food, do evacuations — basically everything they tell me to do. My call sign was invented back during my conscript service because I moved very fast back then”, — recalls “Samolyot”.

“We constantly carry weapons because we are not far from the combat zone, and sabotage and reconnaissance groups can come ‘visiting’. So we always carry an assault rifle — if necessary, we can fire a little”, — he says.
“The most dangerous thing is when they ask you to bring in mines — 120-mm ones — when the entire airborne compartment is loaded with them. The first time I carried 2.5 tons. And the last time I drove to Myrnohrad with mines it was 1.8 tons.
On the way two FPV drones hit us, the brakes failed. But we made it, unloaded.
We didn’t make it back. The vehicle burned down. And we walked home on foot”, — “Samolyot” recalls.

title: “Right now it’s a war of logistics”: on the Lyman direction the enemy is being deprived of supplies and reinforcements
text:
The drone war on the front line is simultaneously a war of logistics.
At present, the main tasks of Ukrainian defenders are to destroy the enemy’s supply lines and preserve their own.
This was stated during an Army TV stream on March 3 by Captain Rostyslav Yashchyshyn, head of the communications department of the 63rd Mechanized Brigade.
“The catalyst for the enemy’s activity is the performance of our unmanned systems. One could say that throughout February the enemy pushed quite actively because our battalion of unmanned systems once again ended up in the top ranks — if I’m not mistaken, in sixth place by the number of enemy forces destroyed.
So we are talking about the fact that they continue to throw large resources in, continue trying to maintain this intensity that is vitally necessary and important for them. But the result is the same.
Even if someone occasionally manages to infiltrate somewhere on the outskirts of Lyman, he will still be destroyed — he will simply live a little longer. But speaking generally about the enemy, they are destroyed every day and in large numbers”, — he said.
Enemy activity remains consistently high and they do not abandon their intentions to capture the city.
“It cannot be said that the enemy has become slower or less active. There is another point worth mentioning, in my opinion. We are now talking not only about a drone war but also about a war of logistics.
We know for sure that the enemy is trying, with the help of various engineering structures, to organize crossings over different water obstacles. Of course we destroy them. But at the same time the enemy does the same.
That is, we also try to create certain engineering structures across water obstacles, and the enemy destroys them in exactly the same way. So now it is a war of logistics. Whoever shows greater ingenuity, a better idea, will be able to use better terrain and win a better foothold for conducting combat operations”, — the serviceman explained.
The officer emphasized that despite the difficult situation, the military firmly holds Lyman and is confident in victory.
“The situation is difficult, of course. It has been difficult for us for three years already. Our brigade has been on the Lyman direction for exactly three years, and it has been difficult since the first day.
And now, with the huge number of drones, it is even harder.
We are trying to hold Lyman. Everyone knows this. But it is difficult to do when the enemy is pushing from different sides.
In essence, we have been holding Lyman for so long, and I hope our guys will not give it up, will not concede it.
Thank God we have enough drones. Our pilots are of a very high level, very highly qualified. As you know, they were recognized by the President of Ukraine for their success.
And in the end, our infantry is not sleeping either, not standing still. We are also developing very actively.
Right now we have a lot of training within the corps. We exchange experience and adopt the best practices.
So we are ready for the fight. No one is going to give up — we will fight to the end and to victory”, — Captain Rostyslav Yashchyshyn emphasized.

title: “War is the will of some kind of chance and, unfortunately, fortune”: the story of a fighter with the call sign “McLaren”
text:
In 2014, due to the occupation of Donetsk, Hennadii “McLaren” moved with his family to the capital, but for years he reproached himself for not staying to fight
The story of the fighter was shared on the page of the 68th Separate Jaeger Brigade named after Oleksa Dovbush of the Air Assault Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
When the full-scale war came in 2022, the successful businessman decided: this time he would not lose everything again.
“I told myself then that my time had come, so on March 6 I was already at the training ground where the 68th Brigade was being formed. That’s how my path in the military began”, — the fighter recalls.
Having joined as a soldier, he ended up in a mortar battery. His call sign came to him from a close comrade whose duties he began to perform — going out to orient the mortar and set up positions.
Since 2023, Hennadii has been the chief sergeant of the “Minotaur” mortar battery.
His responsibilities include training and supporting personnel.
“McLaren” believes that the main task of command is to comprehensively support the warriors who carry out combat missions.
This is exactly how his unit is built — so that comrades feel that they are cared for.
“When two years ago we were redeployed from the Kharkiv region to the Avdiivka direction, I thought: ‘God, how great it is that I will finally defend my home’, because before the war I owned property in Avdiivka.
And I remember the moment when we were still in the area of Semenivka — I saw the pipes of the coke plant through the compass. That image is constantly in my head: I was so happy then that I had the opportunity to defend a place that was very dear to me”, — Hennadii shares.
However, the battles for his small homeland also brought extremely difficult trials.
One of the most tense moments occurred in mid-December 2025, when an enemy guided aerial bomb hit the position and the mortar crew lost communication.
An evacuation group was sent after them and discovered that everyone had been wounded but had survived.
“We were so relieved to hear this news, because we had been preparing for the worst, but we held on to the hope that the guys were still alive. This was one of those rare pleasant moments. But unfortunately there are many others where we cannot influence anything. War is the will of some kind of chance and, unfortunately, fortune. You want to plan everything, but it is not always possible”, — the serviceman says.
In his opinion, war is not only about death but also about life.
Hennadii advises people to prepare themselves to be able to continue living in society with the experience gained, without blaming anyone.
And the greatest motivation for the chief sergeant is his comrades — true friends who are ready to help.
“When they take up their weapons, you understand that this may be their last time going to the position. And the guys trust you and go. So we simply have no right to give up or show that we are tired. Because they believe in you, which means you must also believe in yourself”, — the warrior concluded.

title: “Pantsirs”, “Tors”, “Buks” — these are scarce assets: the sky for manned aviation is cleared by the ‘Luftwaffe’
text:
By knocking out enemy air-defense systems and radars, drone pilots of the Luftwaffe Regiment clear the sky for Ukrainian aviators.
Recently, Luftwaffe Regiment pilots destroyed a Russian Buk system.
Details and the significance of the combat episode were shared during an ArmyTV livestream on March 3 by Major Mykola Kolesnyk, call sign “Tyson”, commander of the 422nd Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment Luftwaffe.
“The target was almost 100 kilometers from the launch line. They felt quite comfortable there, because few operate at such distances.
This Buk had assumed operational duty. Nearby, luckily for us, stood a reloading station, its TZM, but we chose this particular target.
The first strike was to prevent it from driving away and to disable it, and the second strike caused detonation of the warhead mounted on it”, — he said.
Destroying enemy targets at such distances is becoming routine, as the Luftwaffe Regiment operates deep behind enemy lines — including distances beyond 100 km.
“We work both 5 km from the front line and 100+ km deep, carrying out operational-tactical level missions.
When weather permits and there is an opportunity, we work very successfully. We have also directly targeted radar systems.
We have ‘mid-strike’ crews working on infrastructure objects used by the Russian army. And generally, we work on air-defense systems”, — the officer explained.
The Buk is far from the only “trophy” of the Luftwaffe Regiment, as its drone pilots regularly strike infrastructure used by the enemy army and destroy valuable, scarce equipment.
“Before this, we had already struck an S-300 and several enemy tactical-level radars. This segment is one of the leading areas of our regiment.
When you hit a radar or a Buk, you primarily think about diversifying risks for our aviation, which performs very important work.
By destroying enemy air-defense systems, we allow our aviation to work deeper and more safely so they can accomplish their tasks.
It’s not just ‘look, we blew up a Buk, we’re so cool’. No. First of all, we think about how this, in a complex way across the entire axis and to an operational-tactical depth, allows our pilots to work safely — pilots of our aircraft who help hold the frontline and destroy very important targets. This is extremely important”, — Major Mykola Kolesnyk explained.
Among other important tasks of the Luftwaffe Regiment’s drone teams is the fight against Russian drone operators and counter-battery engagements against enemy artillery.
However, knocking out enemy air-defense systems is the top priority, because this inflicts the most painful losses on the Russians.
“Due to sanctions, some types of air-defense systems — I won’t say specifically about the Buk-M1 — but Pantsirs, Tors, have become scarce, hard-to-replace assets.
Every day, when elite SBS crews destroy enemy air-defense systems and radars — this is essentially the core activity that ensures the entire axis can operate safely.
These are scarce assets, they don’t have many, you can’t just buy them in a supermarket”, — the commander of the 422nd Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment Luftwaffe emphasized.

title: “They have deadlines burning in their plans”: on the Pokrovsk axis, Russians assault as soon as the fog settles
text:
On the Pokrovsk axis, Russian occupiers do not reduce pressure on Defense Forces positions and attempt to attack as soon as the fog sets in.
Whether dense fog helps the enemy, was explained in an exclusive comment to ArmyInform by the commander of an operational battalion of the 3rd Operational Brigade named after Colonel Petro Bolbochan “Spartan” of the National Guard of Ukraine, Major Ihor Shafiihulin.
“The enemy has ‘burning deadlines’ in its plans, so they try to conduct assault operations at any cost. Naturally, they try to use changes in weather conditions for this.
Right now is the time when dense fog often covers our axis. So the Russians first try to accumulate manpower and then conduct assaults precisely when the fog settles.
Usually, in fog they try to rush as close as possible to our positions in cars and quad bikes, and then carry out assault actions”, — he said.
However, even the thickest fog cannot prevent Ukrainian defenders from detecting and destroying the occupiers.
“I wouldn’t say that fog critically affects reconnaissance assets or the use of UAVs. As can be seen in videos posted on the brigade’s website and pages, our reconnaissance units and FPV-drone teams work both day and night, both in fog and in rain.
Fog, of course, complicates the process of detecting enemy servicemen somewhat. Overall, when there is fog or precipitation, our reconnaissance tools have a harder job.
However, we can detect and destroy the enemy even in fog.
We strike the enemy both with heavy bombers and various FPV drones. Therefore, we successfully stop and eliminate the enemy. This is one of the indicators of our slogan: ‘The enemy breaks against us!’” — the officer assured.
Currently, enemy activity on the Pokrovsk axis in the area of responsibility of the Spartan Brigade remains consistently high — the enemy tries to assault continuously.
“In general, the number of assault actions and attempts to advance toward our forward edge has not decreased. The enemy continuously conducts offensive and assault operations, trying to infiltrate our combat formations.
Therefore, our brigade constantly inflicts losses on enemy manpower. We also do not forget about their rear — we destroy their tanks and self-propelled artillery systems”, — the officer emphasized.
He reported that only in February, together with neighboring units, the Spartan Brigade eliminated 657 enemy servicemen.
Major Ihor Shafiihulin also provided statistics of enemy losses during the winter months of 2025–2026:
“During the winter period (December, January, February) the Spartan Brigade, together with adjacent units, has the following results:
- 3,553 enemies destroyed;
- 170 Russian servicemen wounded;
- 51 occupiers captured.
Also, 33 quad bikes destroyed and 6 more damaged.
They used motorcycles very little during the winter, so we destroyed only 8 of them.
Ten units of light automotive equipment were destroyed”, — he reported.

title: One year of the “Drone Line”: how $880 million in support enables the elimination of Russians on the frontline
text:
The “Drone Line” is an initiative launched by the President of Ukraine aimed at scaling the most effective UAV units of the Ukrainian military.
This was reported by the Ministry of Defence.
A year ago, the “Drone Line” project — a large-scale program for financing Ukrainian-made UAV procurement for units within the Unmanned Systems Forces — was launched.
The initiative started in March 2025. Its goal is to systematically strengthen the use of UAVs in the Defense Forces, scaling the most effective combat practices and creating sustainable technological superiority on the battlefield.
During this time, the project has become one of the largest foreign direct financing mechanisms for the Ukrainian defense industry in the UAV sector.
The total financing is $880 million with support from the Netherlands. It covers mass procurement of FPV, ISR, and bomber UAVs.
Currently, more than 1,000 crews operate within the initiative. Units of the project eliminate almost every fourth Russian soldier on the frontline, and in January–February — every third.
During the winter alone, the Unmanned Systems Forces, which include “Drone Line” units, incapacitated about 30,000 occupiers.
The project aims to create a zone where the enemy cannot move without losses, while SBS forces can detect and destroy targets before they approach Ukrainian positions.
The development and scaling of the project is a key condition for stopping Russia on land to implement the war plan announced by Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov.
The “Drone Line” demonstrates Ukraine’s shift from fragmented UAV use to a systematic approach, where drones are a full element of defense tactics.
The initiative combines combat experience, technology, and international support, forming a model of modern warfare where technological advantage directly affects battlefield outcomes and saves Ukrainian soldiers’ lives.

“It is important that defenders of life prevail in this confrontation. title: Mutual State Quality Assurance: Ukraine and Finland strengthen defense cooperation
text:
The Ministry of Defence is nearing the final stage of negotiations with Finland on mutual state quality assurance (MSQA) of defense products.
This was reported by the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine on March 3.
It is noted that this is already the eighth such agreement with NATO countries, which will allow Ukrainian arms manufacturers to integrate more quickly into the European market and enable the state to control the quality of foreign procurement according to Alliance standards.
Ukraine and Finland have completed preparatory procedures for signing a Memorandum of Understanding on mutual state quality assurance of defense goods, works, and services.
The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine granted permission for the negotiations and signing.
“Ukraine has already concluded seven such memorandums — with Sweden, the Czech Republic, France, Turkey, Germany, Norway, and Poland. Similar agreements with the United Kingdom, Italy, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Slovenia are being prepared”, — the statement says.
The Ministry noted that the memorandum with Finland will define mechanisms of interaction between the defense agencies of both countries in quality assurance during the implementation of foreign economic contracts.
“This will simplify cooperation procedures between manufacturers, accelerate deliveries, and increase trust in products of the Ukrainian defense-industrial complex”, — the Ministry emphasized.
Under existing agreements, the Ministry of Defence of Ukraine conducts mutual state quality assurance of products under foreign economic contracts with both Ukrainian and foreign manufacturers. This ensures unified approaches to quality control and increases the efficiency of international defense procurement and cooperation.
“Implementation of the agreements will enhance the authority of domestic producers and strengthen international partners’ trust in defense products made in Ukraine”, — said Colonel Yevhen Krasnykov, head of the Main Directorate of State Quality Assurance.

title: NSDC approved energy resilience plans for the regions of Ukraine
text:
At a meeting of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine, comprehensive energy resilience plans for the country’s regions and cities were approved.
This was reported by the Office of the President on March 3.
According to President Volodymyr Zelensky, the experience of this winter will form the basis for further decisions: renewal of infrastructure protection, logistics, key energy facilities, restoration of sites after Russian strikes, and ensuring additional energy capabilities.
During the meeting, representatives of all regions and major cities delivered reports. The NSDC approved resilience plans for each Ukrainian region and regional center except Kyiv. The capital was given additional time to prepare the relevant substantive documents.
“Today, Kyiv was not ready — just as it was not ready for this winter. It must have time to prepare for the next one and fulfill every task. Every city, every Ukrainian community must be prepared for any scenario next winter and to provide real support to the people. The Government of Ukraine, particularly the Ministry of Defense and the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, received the necessary tasks and will help the regions prepare”, — the President emphasized.
NSDC Secretary Rustem Umerov noted that the regional resilience plans include clear instructions for the Cabinet of Ministers and the relevant ministries.
“There must be a clear algorithm: who is responsible, within what time frame, with what resources, and how the implementation is monitored. The NSDC ensures coordination at the state level — meaning regular monitoring. The plans must work in practice. And our task is to ensure that no winter becomes an instrument of pressure on Ukraine”, — Umerov stated.
Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko said that the government will provide protection from UAVs and missiles for major electricity transit, gas extraction, and gas storage facilities. Regions must ensure proper protection of substations, pumping stations, cogeneration facilities, modular boiler houses, and new infrastructure.
“It is important that every city leader, every regional leader, and we as the government bear full personal responsibility for preparing regions and cities for the next heating season. And for fulfilling, failing to fulfill, or untimely fulfilling tasks, we must bear that responsibility”, — Svyrydenko emphasized.
First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy Denys Shmyhal said that the main focus is on restoring the main generation equipment destroyed by the Russians, strengthening the protection of critical infrastructure, creating a reserve of essential equipment, and increasing gas reserves.
“Active work is already underway in all these areas. Regarding the preparation of equipment reserves, we are working with partners to have a threefold stock. Regarding distributed generation, relevant tasks have been assigned to state companies, local administrations, and communities.
At the next ‘Energy Ramstein’ we also plan to discuss attracting over 5 billion euros to prepare Ukraine for the next heating season”, — Shmyhal stated.
Deputy Prime Minister for Restoration and Minister for Communities and Territories Development Oleksii Kuleba noted that the plan approved by the NSDC was developed together with local communities and aims to accelerate change.
“The decision made will have enormous significance for many years ahead. The tasks set today are to do everything possible so that settlements decentralize their water and heat supply systems and become as resilient and adapted to enemy attacks as possible”, — Kuleba summarized.

title: “Guarding the Luhansk NPP” and serving in UAV forces: the Russian army promises “tasty” positions but sends recruits to assault units
text:

But as soon as they sign a contract, they are transferred to assault units — because that’s where the occupation forces suffer the greatest manpower shortage”, — he said.
As previously reported by ArmyInform, fighters of the “Rubizh” Brigade recently captured 20-year-old Serhii from near Yekaterinburg, who was promised service in a UAV unit but found himself in an assault company within a month.
“There’s also a fraud scheme with the upfront payments: in most cases, recruits never receive them because they die in the first month after signing. The money automatically stays on the unit’s balance”, — the officer said.
There are also other schemes enabling Russian commanders to profit off contract soldiers.
“In the 3rd assault company everything is arranged even more ‘beautifully’: after recruits receive part of their upfront payment (300–400 thousand rubles), the commander takes them to a military store that he owns. He advises them to buy clothing because ‘Russian uniforms are crap’. They leave almost all the money there. The remainder is spent on food that will be dropped to them by drones while they move for infiltration”, — the officer shared stories from Russian prisoners.

title: Russia in panic mode: a new wave of fake news about Ukraine amid events in the Middle East
text:
Over the past week, Russia has remained in its usual state — somewhere between hysteria and creative buffoonery.
All because international news suddenly stopped revolving around it, giving way to the escalation in the Middle East.
The propagandists didn’t like that. And, as always, they decided to regain global attention in the only way available to them: by fabricating fakes about Ukraine.
Fake №1: “USA Today found Ukrainian components among missile debris” — only in a parallel universe
A video stylized as USA Today is being massively spread on social networks and pro-Russian trash sites. Allegedly, among the debris of missiles that attacked Israel and U.S. bases, “components of weapons transferred to Ukraine” were “found”.
Sounds dramatic. Truth level: zero.
There is no such “news” on any official USA Today platform. It never existed. And could not exist.
The video is a stitched fake using someone else’s brand — a standard tool of Russian content factories.
Why? To push their favorite narrative once again about a “Ukrainian black market for NATO weapons”.
Yes, the same narrative that regularly collapses when it meets real inspections, international audits, and common sense — but this is propaganda, and propaganda is unfamiliar with common sense.
Fake №2: “Le Point exposed Ukrainian phone scammers who stole €42 million” — yes, but only in an imaginary Paris
The second masterpiece of Russian fantasists is a fake video styled as French Le Point.
According to this fabrication, some “Ukrainian phone scammers” allegedly swindled €42 million from French citizens under the pretext of “raising funds for air defense for French foreign bases”.
On Le Point’s official resources — not a single mention.
The piece was manufactured somewhere in the basements of Russia’s “media combines,” where, judging by the results, the information-front workers seem to operate under heavy doses of creativity-enhancing substances.
What does all this mean?
First: Russia uses any international crisis to smear Ukraine.
Events in the Middle East became the perfect excuse to launch a new wave of disinformation.
The mechanics are simple:
- Take a high-profile event.
- Attach Ukraine to it.
- Spread through anonymous Telegram channels, fake websites, and bot networks.
- Wait for someone to “take the bait.”
The goal is not to inform. The goal is to sow doubt among allies, devalue support, and create an atmosphere of mistrust.
Second: fakes branded as well-known media are a new-old tactic.
Russia has long realized that no one believes its propaganda channels.
So they:
- imitate the style of Western media,
- steal logos,
- forge page layouts,
- use artificially generated anchor voices.
All to create an illusion of “objectivity”. But the illusion collapses at the first check.
Third: Russia is nervous.
If everything were going well, they wouldn’t have to invent “Ukrainian missiles” in Israel or “€42 million” in an imaginary French underworld.
A country confident in its position does not generate dozens of fakes per day. Only a panicking one does.
Propaganda fails again, but attempts will continue
Russia’s new “exposés” are nothing but another set of cheap productions.
Fake videos, fabricated statements, forged brands.
All this for one purpose — to damage Ukraine’s reputation and undermine partner support.
But the world has already learned to recognize Russian fake “masterpieces”.
And the more the Kremlin lies, the louder the truth sounds — about who actually threatens international security.

pairs.question: How is Russian disinformation used to target international support for Ukraine?
pairs.answer: Russia exploits global crises to launch disinformation campaigns that falsely link Ukraine to illegal activities, such as the black market for weapons, in an effort to erode trust among allies and devalue international support.
pairs.stance_statement: Russian disinformation is framed as a malicious tool designed to undermine the necessary international support and military aid for Ukraine.

title: Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine thanked the Netherlands for its leadership role in the Fighter Jet Coalition
text:
General Oleksandr Syrskyi held a substantive meeting with the Chief of Defence of the Armed Forces of the Netherlands, General Onno Eichelsheim.
This was reported in a statement by Oleksandr Syrskyi.
In General Eichelsheim, he expressed his sincere gratitude to the army, government, and people of the Netherlands for their consistent support of Ukraine in its resistance against the Russian aggressor.
Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion by the Russian Federation, the Dutch government has allocated €20.8 billion to strengthen Ukraine.
Particularly important is the Netherlands’ contribution of €750 million to the PURL initiative for financing purchases of American weaponry.
The Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine also thanked the Netherlands for its leadership role in the Fighter Jet Coalition, particularly for transferring F-16 aircraft to Ukraine.
Efforts are now underway regarding the readiness of Dutch partners to provide Ukraine with simulators for these fighter jets.
General Oleksandr Syrskyi informed him about the operational and strategic situation at the front.
Despite significant personnel and equipment losses, the Russian aggressor refuses to abandon offensive actions.
By the end of the year, the Kremlin plans to recruit more than 400,000 contract soldiers to increase its contingent in Ukraine to 800,000 servicemembers.
Therefore, we have no choice but to continue the fight and destroy the enemy.
Oleksandr Syrskyi informed his Dutch counterpart about the priority needs of the Armed Forces of Ukraine for repelling the Russian onslaught. These include, above all, air defense systems and various types of missile weaponry.
“I am confident in the effectiveness of further military cooperation in accordance with the national interests of Ukraine, the Netherlands, and other NATO member states, in order to strengthen the security of the entire European space”, — Oleksandr Syrskyi stated.
As a symbol of gratitude for productive cooperation and his personal contribution to Ukraine’s resilience, Oleksandr Syrskyi presented General Onno Eichelsheim with the highest distinction of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine — the honorary badge Cross of Merit.

title: “They Listen to Us and Hear Us”: Head of Public Council on Meeting With Ministry of Defense Representatives
text:
Representatives of the Ministry of Defense met with members of the Public Council at the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War.
The meeting was also attended by representatives of the Coordination Headquarters and the Office of the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights.
They discussed optimal models for the operation of Social Support Centers, which are intended to provide comprehensive assistance and support to families of missing servicemembers.
The head of the Public Council at the Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War, Iryna Abramova, expressed satisfaction that the Ministry of Defense listens to the council’s members:
“We are pleased that they hear us. We are satisfied that the Standard Regulation will be changed, that the public opinion —‘do not change what already works well’— will be taken into account. And most importantly, we hope these changes will take place”.
Abramova added that council members also expect that regulatory documents will first be put in order, and afterward the Social Support Centers will begin functioning.
“We agreed that the Centers will work with servicemembers of those military units that were disbanded, and whose documents were transferred to the Territorial Recruitment and Social Support Centers. These servicemembers’ documents will be moved to the Support Centers, the first of which has been established in the western region.
We consider this a sound agreement and sound cooperation. And we hope this cooperation will continue”, — said Abramova.
“We reached an understanding that at present the Social Support Center will focus on working with documents of military units that are being disbanded or have already been disbanded. In particular, these are rifle battalions whose successors are the TRCC and SSC.
We also agreed on the need to amend the Standard Regulation on the Center to clarify the Center’s tasks concerning the search for missing persons”, — emphasized Colonel Oleksandr Pukhalskyi, Deputy Director of the Department of Social Support of the Ministry of Defense.

title: Military Expert Explains Consequences of Israel–US War Against Iran
text:
The war of Israel and the United States against Iran has both advantages and disadvantages for Ukraine. The negative side is that oil prices will rise, but this
Military expert, Colonel Petro Chernyk, stated this on Army FM.
“America is currently the world’s leading producer of shale oil, and if this does not harm them, they will be able to establish — even at a critical moment— conditional oil supplies by tankers to Europe, because liquefied gas has in fact been supplied for several years already. But here is a downside for us: we remember that the entire Russian economy rests on its backbone — hydrocarbons.
So they will indeed benefit for some time, but not strategically or critically. The Druzhba oil pipeline is halted as such. And the Europeans, again, will readjust their supplies, possibly from America, and Norwegians will certainly begin producing some share of the oil”, — he said.
According to him, this will give Russia more currency, which it uses to purchase microelectronics, including for missiles. A single “Kinzhal” contains 130 Western components.
“The truth is that this is also a very ambiguous issue, because 80% of the entire flow of microelectronics — including black-market technologies—went through Iran, and that channel is now definitely closed as of this moment. Will the Russians manage to rebuild their supply chains? They will, but it will take several months. Several months — and everything has already become an order of magnitude more expensive for them since 2022, and this will increase prices even more”, — the military expert said.
In Petro Chernyk’s opinion, it is very good that the US and Israel struck the key link in the ‘axis of evil’ triangle — China–Iran–Russia.
He added that the Americans also realized they need to demonstrate their strength to China, which is seriously considering the seizure of Taiwan.

title: Ukrainian Team Wins International NATO Hackathon
text:
Officers of the Department of Computer Science and Intelligent Technologies of VITI demonstrated an outstanding result at the NATO TIDE Hackathon 2026.

The developed prototype has the potential to become the basis for Next Generation Targeting, one of ACT’s key projects aimed at achieving the Alliance’s technological advantage.

title: Slaves of Occupation and a Verdict That Brought Justice Closer
text:
After Russian forces entered Tokmak, they broke more than just the city physically.
Here, in the heart of the temporarily occupied city, on the grounds of the former police station, a real torture chamber emerged.
In these walls, in small cells without ventilation, without water, without light, without beds, 8–14 people lived side by side. They slept on the floor, drank water by opening a hose from the toilet tank. They inhaled suffocation. Endured pain. And waited in uncertainty.
And it was there that four individuals — Ukrainian citizens who voluntarily became executioners of their own people — operated.
More detailed information about these traitors has been published in the Book of Executioners of the Ukrainian People.
Who They Are: Those Who Betrayed Their Homeland
oleksii koshel (born 1974)
Headed the occupation “Department of Internal Affairs” of Tokmak.
A former police major — a person who should have protected citizens.
Instead — he ordered deportations, coordinated the isolation unit, and launched the torture chamber at full scale.
mykhailo vydysh (born 1991)
Head of the isolation unit. He decided who would dig trenches that day, who would be sent for interrogation, and who — for another “punishment session”.
Personally prepared deportations.
A former senior police lieutenant.
andrii koshel (born 1991)
Duty officer. Escorted and beat prisoners. Took people for slave labor.
A former sergeant of the internal service.
At the time of the verdict, he already had a 14-year sentence for collaborationism. It wasn’t enough — he received another.
mykola dereza (born 1971)
Senior escort officer. Beat people. Humiliated them. Took people to dig trenches.
A former police warrant officer.
He also had previously received a 14-year sentence — and now again appears on the list of convicted individuals.
The Isolation Unit as a Tool of Terror: A Chronicle of Brutality
After the occupation, the old police station was turned into a private torture chamber.
Here people were forced to “confess” to anything.
Interrogations were conducted both by the collaborators themselves and by FSB investigators. They beat people with rifle butts, used electric shocks, staged executions, threatened to kill and bury them in nameless pits, and demanded confessions of cooperation with the SSU or the Armed Forces.
Yet most detainees were ordinary people — workers, drivers, teachers.
Ukrainians the Occupiers Tried to Turn into Slaves
Since October 2022, the isolation unit became an endless reserve of free labor for the Russian occupation army.
Every morning, the duty officer read the list.
Groups of 14–15 people were taken outside the city.
At gunpoint, accompanied by dog handlers and dogs, people dug trenches and dugouts for hours, days, weeks.
For an escape attempt, everyone was punished: forced to squat until total exhaustion, until their legs gave out.
Some Were “Deported” Only to Be Captured Again
This so-called “release” was a farce.
The head of the isolation unit tied people’s hands with tape, covered their faces with a bag, took them to a checkpoint, and read a “deportation order” on camera.
These videos later appeared on Russian propaganda channels, including “Russia-24”.
Then came the forced march toward Ukrainian-controlled territory — for 2–6 hours under threat of being shot.
Some people still ended up captured again — and spent months digging trenches on the front line.
A woman who refused to dig was sent to a minefield.
What happened to her — no one knows.
This crime still awaits investigation.
The Day Justice Stood Tall
On May 19, 2025, the Khortytskyi District Court delivered its verdict.
After an appeal, the court in the city of Zaporizhzhia upheld it.
- oleksii koshel — 12 years.
Stripped of his police major rank. 3-year ban on holding positions. - mykhailo vydysh — 12 years.
Stripped of rank. Restrictions on holding positions. - andrii koshel — 11 years.
Combined with his previous sentence — 15 years. Property confiscation. - mykola dereza — 11 years.
Combined — also 15 years with confiscation.
These verdicts are a signal to those who still believe that occupation is eternal, that crimes will go unpunished, that cruelty can be hidden in darkness.
No — it will not work.
Every executioner sooner or later hears the footsteps of justice.
The Ukrainian state is returning its lands.
And with them — the right to punish everyone who dared trample human dignity.
You may hide behind someone else’s insignia, you may change your place of residence, you may flee deeper into Russia.
But you will not escape the truth, the law, or the memory of the people you beat, broke, tortured.
Your names are already recorded.
The facts exist.
The testimonies are collected.
Justice is coming.
And it will find every one of you.

title: Countering Russian UAVs: Oleksandr Syrskyi Updates on Implementation of Anti-Drone Protection Projects
text:
The Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, General Oleksandr Syrskyi, held a working meeting on “small air defense”.
He reported this on March 3 on social media.
According to the Commander-in-Chief, the key role in this counteraction is shifting to interceptor UAVs.
For example, in Kyiv and its outskirts, such interceptor drones accounted for more than 70% of downed “Shaheds” in February.
During the meeting on “small air defense”, the results of fulfilling tasks at the first, second, and third tiers of intercepting enemy “Shaheds” were analyzed.
General Oleksandr Syrskyi heard reports on the implementation of the project to strengthen anti-drone protection of key administrative centers across Ukraine, on upgrading army aviation helicopters for better countering “Shaheds,” and more.
— Despite the significant deterioration in weather conditions and the shortage of means of destruction, we did not allow a decline in “small air defense” performance in February, — Syrskyi noted.
According to him, over the past month Ukrainian interceptor drones carried out about 6,300 sorties, destroying over 1,500 Russian UAVs of various types.
— We are searching for and finding answers to the new tactics of using “Shaheds” at extremely low altitudes. We are working with manufacturers to increase the effectiveness of various interceptor drone models. We continue forming and training UAV crews. We are equipping air-defense units of unmanned systems, — Syrskyi emphasized.
He added that a significant amount of work has been completed over the past year, but efforts must be intensified and accelerated — as this is primarily about protecting peaceful Ukrainian cities and villages, Ukraine’s energy system, and other rear infrastructure.
Following the meeting, the Commander-in-Chief assigned tasks to the relevant military-command bodies, including the newly established ones.
General Oleksandr Syrskyi thanked everyone involved in strengthening Ukraine’s air shield and destroying the enemy.

title: The Government Has Improved the Mechanisms for Involving Volunteer Formations in Air Defense
text:
The main task of such groups has been defined as countering air threats, including enemy strike unmanned aerial vehicles.
This was reported on March 3 by the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine.
At the initiative of the Ministry of Defense, the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine approved amendments to the resolution regulating the implementation of the experimental project to strengthen air defense (AD) by involving volunteer formations of territorial communities (VFTC).
The goal is to improve the mechanisms for involving volunteers and increase the overall effectiveness of countering air threats amid intensified enemy air attacks.
The adopted document removes a number of organizational barriers and clarifies the requirements for training the personnel who defend the Ukrainian sky. The changes concern several key areas:
More initiative for military command on the ground.
From now on, the right to initiate the creation of air defense groups within the VFTC structure belongs not only to the heads of military administrations. This authority is expanded to include commanders of VFTC and commanders of military units of the Territorial Defense Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine to which the respective volunteer formation is subordinated.
At the same time, the mandatory participation of the head of the military administration in determining the commander of such an AD group is excluded from the procedure.
Clear personnel criteria.
The newly created AD groups will include VFTC members who, in accordance with Article 23 of the Law of Ukraine “On Mobilization Training and Mobilization”, have a deferment from conscription. A mandatory condition is specialized training and obtaining a certificate as an external drone pilot, technician, or sapper.
Professional certification of specialists.
Operators (external pilots) of unmanned aerial vehicles must obtain a certificate from educational institutions (centers or schools) certified directly by the Ministry of Defense.
Sappers included in these groups must undergo training at institutions of the Ministry of Defense, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, or the State Emergency Service and receive an official state sapper qualification.
Temporary reinforcement by Territorial Defense Forces specialists.
If there are not enough individuals among volunteers with the qualifications of pilot, technician, or sapper, it is permitted to temporarily involve active-duty servicemembers of the Territorial Defense Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine with the appropriate specialty.
Unified control and compatibility.
The created groups will operate as an integrated part of the general air defense system of the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Operational planning and direct control of their actions will remain under the exclusive competence of the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine through the relevant air defense command bodies.
The approved amendments eliminate unnecessary bureaucracy and give commanders the necessary flexibility in managing units. Implementation of the innovations will significantly enhance the ability of local communities to protect their airspace.
In June 2025, the Government approved a resolution on the implementation of an experimental project to create air defense groups formed from members of volunteer territorial community formations.
The main task of such groups has been defined as countering air threats, particularly enemy strike UAVs.

title: The vehicle flew like in the Paris–Dakar Rally: combat medic “Hannibal” tells the story of a rescued wounded soldier
text:
He began his service back in 2017 in the National Guard of Ukraine, signed a contract, and fought in assault units near Avdiivka and in the Luhansk region.
The story of the combat medic was shared on the page of the 41st Separate Mechanized Brigade of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
Several enemy FPV drones hit a vehicle carrying soldiers to their positions. One of the men received a severe injury. Luckily, at that moment, the senior combat medic of the 41st Brigade’s mechanized company, call sign “Hannibal”, was on duty.
“The soldier had multiple shrapnel wounds on the right side of the body — from the elbow joint to the thigh. We counted about 15 wounds, and another fragment struck the groin area. There was heavy bleeding.
My comrade — also the company’s senior combat medic — and I immediately began applying tamponade and bandages. The sky above us was literally swarming with enemy drones. One UAV attempted to attack us. But our soldier shot it down in the darkness. We managed to get the wounded man into a basement”, — he recalls.
“Hannibal” and his comrade took care of the soldier for a full day under constant shelling. Eventually, the wounded fighter was evacuated to safety.
“Hannibal” recalls that the vehicle “flew like in the Paris–Dakar Rally”, and the men could barely stay in the truck bed. But everything turned out well.
The combat medic says the soldier survived thanks to timely first aid. He insists there was nothing heroic — he simply did what he had to.
“Hannibal” is an experienced serviceman from the Donetsk region. He began his service in 2017 in the National Guard of Ukraine.
Later he suffered a severe spinal fracture and, after long rehabilitation and treatment, was forced to leave the service.
He returned to duty after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. He also managed to evacuate his family to Kharkiv from his hometown, which is now almost destroyed by continuous fighting.
“At first, I served in mobile fire groups that destroyed enemy drones, and later I joined the 41st Brigade. At first, I was a rifleman and fought in the Kursk region. Then I mastered tactical medicine. I find it interesting”, — he says.
According to him, when he first joined the service, no one knew anything about modern tourniquets or the MARCH algorithm.
He plans to continue his military service and study further. “Hannibal” also enjoys cooking — unsurprising, as his civilian specialty is culinary. He gladly cooks borscht, cheese soup, and sushi for the guys — and even fried potatoes for them right on positions.

title: The government has strengthened the capabilities of private air-defense groups to protect critical infrastructure
text:
The Government has adopted a decision that strengthens the capabilities of air-defense groups established at enterprises.
This was announced by the Minister of Defense of Ukraine Mykhailo Fedorov on March 2.
He recalled that in November last year the Government allowed the launch of an experimental project involving enterprises in the state air-defense system. At that time, enterprises were given the opportunity to create their own air-defense groups integrated into the unified command system of the Air Force.
“Now we are taking the next step — expanding their capabilities. The Government has adopted a decision that strengthens the capabilities of air-defense groups created at enterprises,” the statement reads.
Key changes:
- Enterprises will be able to temporarily receive weapons and means of destruction from the warehouses of military units of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, provided these assets are not used in combat units.
- The list of means and the amount of ammunition will be determined by the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine within an individual decision for each enterprise.
- In case they are used while repelling attacks, resupply will be carried out under a simplified procedure based on an act of actual expenditure.
According to the minister, the transfer of weapons will take place exclusively for the duration of the experimental project and only with the approval of the Air Force Command.
This mechanism makes it possible to promptly strengthen the protection of critical infrastructure facilities and integrate private capabilities into the state’s unified air-defense system.
“Protecting the sky is a top priority defined by the President of Ukraine. Our goal is to identify 100% of air threats in real time and intercept at least 95% of missiles and drones.
We have already implemented the After Action Review system to analyze attacks, established the command of the ‘small’ air-defense system, and developed a concept for systematic protection from Shaheds, which we are gradually implementing”, — Mykhailo Fedorov emphasized.
Coordination between the Air Force, military administrations, and the new command has also been established. Regional leaders are now able to analyze the effectiveness of air defense in real time.
“We are uniting all levels of command to strengthen the protection of our sky”, — the minister summarized.

title: Telemedicine can be an additional tool for reducing AWOL risks — Oleksandr Syrskyi
text:

The meeting also considered proposals from the Medical Forces Command regarding increasing the amount of telemedicine equipment and expanding the list of units where it is used.
“I support the implementation of these measures.
We also addressed the issue of physical recovery of servicemen after completing combat missions, taking into account the practical experience of the 412th Nemesis drone brigade.

title: Ukrainian forces have already liberated 9 settlements in the Oleksandrivka direction
text:

“The units of the AAF grouping are relentlessly pressing the enemy, liberating Ukrainian land, destroying the occupiers, and methodically cutting their logistical arteries. During the operation, the enemy is being systematically and decisively pushed out of fortified positions. Targeted and massive strikes are destroying the occupiers’ manpower, weapons, military and special equipment.

Since the beginning of the operation, since 29 January 2026, the enemy has lost 6,537 personnel, including:

In addition, the occupiers have lost 419 units of weapons and military equipment, including 14 armored fighting vehicles and 7 tanks.

title: “Even in war, there are many smiles and funny moments”: the story of a medic with the call sign “Ninja”
text:
Eduard Revin, call sign “Ninja”, is a medical orderly of a mechanized battalion of the 23rd brigade, originally from Donetsk region.
His story was published on the page of the 23rd Separate Mechanized Brigade of the 20th Army Corps of the Ground Forces of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
In civilian life, he studied to be a paramedic in Makiivka and worked in a hospital and the Synlab medical laboratory.
As a displaced person from Donetsk region, he temporarily lived in Dnipro. That is where his military journey began. He received a draft notice on the street, passed the medical examination, and when asked whether he was willing to serve, replied that if needed — then yes.
He has served since January 2023 and says he does not regret being assigned specifically to the 23rd brigade.
He knows well the difference between “peace medicine” and “war medicine”: at the front, he sees severe wounds and amputations.
“The picture is sad, but we have no other choice. And even in war, there are many smiles and funny moments. I believe this is a protective reaction to stress and everything we see. We try to shield ourselves with humor, to cheer each other up a bit”, — he says.
The medic describes evacuations and how they depend on the situation: sometimes comrades bring the wounded to designated points in armored vehicles, sometimes it is medics with their own transport.
He recalls helping civilians after shelling — for example, after the shelling of a village council, where military medics assisted the injured.
Eduard also speaks of the occupation of his home village: enemies near the house, bullet-riddled doors, a killed dog, looting.
Residents managed to escape from Velyka Novosilka in Donetsk region only when the enemy’s checkpoint was empty.
Eduard concludes: the enemy will stop only where we stop him. And to those who hesitate, he answers simply: “If you don’t know how to do something — the Armed Forces of Ukraine will teach you”.

title: “They tried to distract UAV operators”: the enemy used two tanks in a “reconnaissance by combat” attempt
text:
With changing weather, Russians began using armored vehicles more actively. Depending on their tasks, they equip them with various additional protections.
This was reported to ArmyInform by the Phoenix Main Department of Unmanned Aerial Systems of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine.
“In the second half of February, the enemy somewhat increased the activity of its heavy armored vehicles, particularly in Donetsk region.
Our Phoenix pilots observed isolated raids of individual armored vehicles in their areas of responsibility on the Toretsk and Pokrovsk directions”, — the unit noted.
Earlier, ArmyInform published a video showing Phoenix pilots destroying two Russian tanks on the Toretsk direction.
Interestingly, the armored vehicles had different types of protection and, judging by everything, different tasks.
“We note in this case an attempt at ‘reconnaissance by combat’ with two tanks, although we have also encountered MT-LBs, APCs, BMPs.
In the video, we see a pair of tanks performing reconnaissance by combat. One of them is disguised with a white camouflage net to blend into the snow. It follows at some distance behind the first tank, which has more welded-on protection — chains, rods, nets.
We can conclude that the enemy tried to distract the UAV operators of the Defense Forces with the first tank, while the second under its cover was supposed to perform another function, likely delivering personnel to positions.
However, the enemy failed to execute its plan, and both tanks were destroyed. As seen, Phoenix pilots first immobilized the vehicles, then systematically worked on both tanks until they were completely burned. It was crucial for us to destroy the equipment so no one could use it again”, — the unit said.
Phoenix links this enemy activity to weather changes: warmer conditions made the ground less passable for vehicles such as cars, ATVs, or motorcycles.
However, the need for logistics missions remained, so Russians began using armored vehicles that had been accumulating over winter months.
“We wouldn’t call this a new tactic. It is more a correction to current conditions. Nothing new — we saw the same a year ago.
After this small surge in activity, we expect another stall: once the ground dries and weather improves, more maneuverable means — ATVs, motorcycles, electric scooters — will be used again”, — Phoenix noted.

title: “We will fight for the life of every warrior”: the Minister of Defense announced the start of an audit of frontline losses
text:
In 2026, the scaling-up of ground robotic systems will take place so that it is the GRS that perform logistics tasks.
Minister of Defense of Ukraine Mykhailo Fedorov wrote about this on his page on March 2.
Last week, he spent several days working directly on the frontline with mechanized, air-assault brigades and air-defense units. The goal is to synchronize decisions to strengthen defense and systematically prepare for spring.
Key priorities:
- strengthening tactical and operational depth;
- scaling drones and interceptors;
- protecting logistics and critical routes;
- completing brigade manning;
- deploying additional air-defense groups;
- developing electronic warfare and radar coverage;
- expanding fortifications.
The Minister of Defense said that work is currently underway in several directions.
Launch of the basic minimum for brigade drone supplies
This means guaranteed monthly supplies of FPV drones, reconnaissance drones, bombers, and other UAVs—in addition to state deliveries, eDrones and other purchases.
“This will allow brigades to plan their defense and be confident in their resources. We are also working on centralized supplying of Starlinks and pickups for the army”, —Mykhailo Fedorov noted.
Audit of losses
According to the minister, the analysis of every loss on the battlefield is beginning.
“The audit will help identify key problems and make management decisions to resolve them systematically. Human capital is the highest value. We will fight for the life of every warrior”, — he emphasized.
Changing the approach to forming requirements
“In the near future, we will move from manually forming needs to an automated model. Based on high-quality frontline data, we will form real requirements without a ‘zoo’ of ineffective solutions. Our goal is for the military to receive the best solutions rather than having to refine them with their own hands in the trenches”, — the minister stated.
Review of annual drone supply targets
“A procurement plan has been formed. There will be more interceptors, FPV drones, fiber-optic drones, wing-type reconnaissance drones, long-range strike drones, and other necessary equipment. The first quarter is already contracted: for the first time, need was formed based on data, eliminating subjective influence and corruption risks. Procurement results will soon be felt at the front”, — said Mykhailo Fedorov.
Scaling of ground robotic systems (GRS)
This year, there will be many more ground robotic complexes. The goal is to transfer logistics to GRS to reduce personnel losses.
An alternative to ‘Maviks’
“We are working on products that can be analogues of Mavics, using AI. We are already testing solutions that will soon be scaled up on the frontline”, — Mykhailo Fedorov assured.

title: Rescue of Private “Spartak”: A Ground Robotic Complex Evacuated a Wounded Soldier From a Mined Area
text:
Ukrainian defenders used a ground robotic system to save Private “Spartak,” who stepped on a mine.
The corresponding video appeared on the channel of the 1st Separate Medical Battalion.
“During the preparation of positions, the wounded soldier was spotted by an enemy reconnaissance drone. Due to the exposure, they decided to change positions, but during the relocation, they triggered a mine”, — the defenders reported.
As a result of the explosion, the soldier sustained multiple shrapnel wounds to his lower limbs and could not move on his own.
“A remote telemedicine consultation was provided to his comrades to deliver urgent care and stabilize the wounded soldier — including wound packing”, — the military noted.
They then decided to evacuate him using the robotic system. The evacuation was complicated by dense mining of the area, requiring additional reconnaissance and careful movement. The mission lasted 5 hours and 15 minutes.
Throughout the evacuation, communication with the wounded soldier was maintained via the internal audio system inside the robot’s capsule.
After extraction from the “kill zone”, he was transferred to a medical evacuation team and then safely transported to forward surgical groups, where he received all necessary medical care. He is now continuing treatment at the next stage.
“Remote telemedicine assistance helps win time for the wounded to await evacuation. Providing voice support helps maintain moral and psychological stability”, — the battalion stated.
The ground robotic complex evacuated the wounded despite attacks by Russian FPV drones.

title: If a Commander Is Not Confident in His Actions, His People Will See It: The Story of Commander Callsign “Vedeha”
text:
The soldier “Vedeha” is an infantryman. He chose the warrior’s path in his youth, received a military education, and joined the Armed Forces of Ukraine. He has
His story was shared on the page of the 33rd Separate Mechanized Brigade of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
“My first combat experience was as part of a reconnaissance platoon near Troitske in Luhansk Oblast. We were told an enemy sabotage-reconnaissance group had approached one of our positions. We went out searching for the enemy, walked ten kilometers. The enemy tried to drive us out with a mortar and snipers, but we successfully hid in a low spot. We detected the saboteurs — and returned without losses”, — the soldier recalls.
They worked in small groups, doing everything possible to hinder the enemy.
“It was interesting work. We constantly moved toward the enemy. Conducted reconnaissance and mining. Carried out sabotage missions. Placed Ukrainian flags to hit the enemy morally — to show that we were nearby even if they couldn’t see us”, — says Vedeha.
The experienced scout was sent for training at a military academy. Then came the first day of the full-scale invasion.
“We woke up in the barracks on the training ground, hearing: it’s begun. As someone with combat experience, I was ready to be sent to fight at any moment. And they indeed sent us to defend Lviv airport — it was likely the enemy would try to land forces there”, — he says.
Later, he returned to his studies, finished early, and went to defend Kyiv.
“I ended up in a mobile anti-tank group. As a commander, I was told: go pick your soldiers. I chose thirty. They gave us quad bikes and told us: here is the defense sector — all directions where the enemy might try to break through with tanks must be controlled. And in case of an enemy offensive — we were to destroy the tanks”, — the soldier recounts.
Later, he took command of a company and moved to Maiorske in Donetsk Oblast.
“I’m glad I have the combat experience of a soldier. My soldiers understood I knew what I was doing — and followed me. We held that area for four months — and left without a single casualty”, — says Vedeha.
He commanded battles, personally evacuated the wounded. He suffered multiple injuries and blast traumas. He could have transferred to a rear unit but chose to continue serving in the combat-ready 33rd Brigade.
“Arms and legs are intact — that means I can fight. I went on to be more useful to Ukraine and our Victory. Now I oversee combat training of soldiers before they head to positions”, — he explains.
The most important trait of a commander, he says, is self-confidence.
“If a commander is not confident in his actions, his people will see it — and won’t be confident in what they themselves must do. If a commander has no combat experience, he won’t lead well. Until you go through it yourself, you understand nothing. All decisions must be made with a cool head — consider all risks and do nothing impulsively”, — he says.
Convincing soldiers of their own strength is another key duty.
“Almost everyone is afraid at first: how can you just go to fight. The first time is scary. So I tell them my own example. I say: guys, when I went, I was scared too, it was just as hard for me. I tell them what I went through, how I acted. I show by my own life — how and in what situations we operated. Then people begin to work properly”, — the soldier emphasizes.
That is how — confidently and with a cold mind — Victory will be won.
“Victory for me will come when my children grow up in safety, and I know no missiles or Shaheds are flying at them — and no Russian will come to kill them. When we drive out the enemy and he capitulates — realizing that we are unbeatable”, — the soldier concluded.

A period of intensive ballistic missile use. On January 9, the main strike focused on Kyiv Oblast (278 targets). A medium-range ballistic missile strike on Lviv Oblast was recorded, as well as the use of Zircons on January 20 and 24.
February 2026

The enemy is systematically increasing the use of both standard ballistic missiles (Iskander-M) and missiles approaching the target along a ballistic trajectory: Kinzhal, Zircon, Kh-22/32, S-300/S-400. In total, over three months the aggressor launched more than 700 missiles of various types.
“Despite these challenges, Ukraine’s sky held. The energy system was preserved thanks to the professionalism of the anti-aircraft missile forces, mobile fire groups, radio-technical units, and aviation. Each intercepted missile is proof that we have become stronger, more technologically advanced, and more experienced.
At the same time, we thank every energy worker and repair crew who, under fire, restored power and kept the grid alive. Combat work continues. We know the enemy is preparing new attacks, but every unit of our air defense remains on full combat readiness.
